briefing: A real snapshot of the air over the Strait of Hormuz, as the public ADS-B network saw it on 6 November 2026, 19:02 UTC. 137 aircraft are on the map, 137 of them civil airliners and cargo flights. You are the observer: every aircraft is listed under FORCES, click one to see its call sign, type, heading and altitude, and speed up time to watch the traffic move. The AD, RADAR and NUC buttons show the air-defence and radar sites around the strait. Nothing here shoots: all sides start weapons-hold and there is nothing to win or lose. REAL snapshot taken 2026-11-06 19:02Z (UTC) from public ADS-B data (adsb.lol, ODbL). 137 contacts: 0 mapped to platform-DB types, 137 UNKNOWN. Sides Neutral 137. Aircraft start where the network saw them, on their reported heading, speed and altitude. UNKNOWN contacts (type not in the platform database) are unarmed Neutral traffic and take no part in combat; all sides start weapons-hold. Sources: adsb.lol /v2/mil USED; adsb.lol /v2/point USED; AISStream SKIPPED (AISStream requires an API key; no keyless AIS source covers this bbox). ESTIMATED: positions are one receiver-network snapshot; sides come from the ICAO address block (state of registry), not the operator; types are matched by ICAO designator only (a family, not a variant); aircraft hold course and speed, no flight plans. Ships are not included. Full limitations and counts are in the scenario's snapshot block.

limitations: ESTIMATED: positions, altitudes, speeds and headings are one ADS-B receiver-network snapshot (adsb.lol); aircraft with transponders off or no coverage are absent, and military aircraft often fly without broadcasting.

ESTIMATED: side assignment uses the ICAO 24-bit address block (state of registry), not the operator or flag. Coalition = US, GB, FR, DE, IT, NL, CA, AU registry; Iran = Iranian registry; every other military aircraft is Neutral.

ESTIMATED: platform mapping is by ICAO type designator only (a family, not a variant): E2 -> E-2C, H60 -> SH-60B, F14 -> F-14A/D. Aircraft with no exact match are UNKNOWN contacts (generic unarmed placeholder, Neutral side).
Ships are not included: AISStream requires an API key; no keyless AIS source covers this bbox.
Aircraft fly straight on their snapshot heading and speed; there is no flight-plan data, so they leave the theater.
No military aircraft were visible on ADS-B inside the box at fetch time (none is not the same as none flying).
Civil aircraft are included as Neutral UNKNOWN contacts (137); they carry the real transponder type code but no platform record.
